candidates.requirement: Exercise the default-enabled reparse deferral mechanism for a partial XML token through successive nonfinal parse calls on the same parser.
candidates.target_route: A finite XML document with a long token can be split across nonfinal XML_Parse calls; after the first incomplete-token attempt, a later small nonfinal increment with buffer capacity available can make have_now less than twice had_before and defer processing.
candidates.failure_condition: ParseOneInput passes all bytes once with isFinal=0 and then all bytes again with isFinal=1. The first call starts with had_before=0, so it cannot defer; the second call bypasses the deferral guard because finalBuffer is true. The entry repeats this pattern on freshly created parsers.
candidates.alternative_paths: The namespace and external parsers use the same helper sequence. External parser creation copies the enabled setting but initializes a fresh partial-token count. Zero-length input, reset, and the final call provide no equivalent later nonfinal attempt.

before.requirement: Exercise default-enabled reparse deferral after an incomplete-token attempt.
before.reason: The before source calls the processor directly and has no callProcessor definition, so this same deferral behavior did not yet exist.

source_evidence.quote: Verified preimage file expat/lib/xmlparse.c has no function definition named callProcessor. The entire after definition consists of added lines. This establishes absence in this file only; other implementations or equivalent paths must still be considered.

after.requirement: Exercise the default-enabled deferral branch through successive nonfinal parse calls on one parser after an incomplete token.
after.reason: The new helper can defer only after an earlier partial-token attempt while finalBuffer is false. Each target parser gets one nonfinal call followed by a final call.

claims.reason: The innermost blocking condition is the new helper's requirement for a later nonfinal attempt with insufficient added data. That condition did not exist before; the before code invoked the processor directly. The same old harness therefore has an introduced coverage gap for this tuple.
